summary: Phase 3 Operations module (8 backend endpoints + 5 frontend pages + secondary sidebar) tested end-to-end. Backend: 20 passed / 1 skipped (seeding gap, see below) in new pytest suite test_phase3_operations.py. Frontend: every required data-testid renders, the magic-link auth works (cookie + 303), CSV download triggers, the row→lifecycle navigation works, the failed-tx retry flow POSTs and returns 200, all 11 funds widgets render with real values, treemap + volume table render with delta arrows + share bars, sidebar nav works between all 4 sub-pages. No HIGH-priority bugs found in this module.

minor.issue: Any unknown @prosper.foundation email is AUTO-PROVISIONED with role=super_admin on first login (server.py L192 and L239). This means ops@prosper.foundation / compliance@prosper.foundation / support@prosper.foundation cannot be used to assert the 403 path on POST /admin/transactions/{id}/retry-step — they all log in as super_admin instead of admin/compliance_officer/support as documented in /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Either (a) seed those staff users with their intended roles in seed.py so future role-check tests work, or (b) lock auto-provisioning of @prosper.foundation to role=admin (not super_admin) and require explicit promotion. Did not block this iteration but limits role-based test coverage.

issues: Visual inspection only showed 1 row visible in tbody on initial render — the by-client backend stats endpoint returns many orgs (verified in pytest). Could be a CSS overflow / DataTable virtualization issue. Worth a manual eyeball to confirm — was not the focus of this iteration so flagged as low-priority for follow-up.

A large number of rows in the table show the org name as the generic 'TEST Holdings' (leftover from earlier onboarding tests). Not a bug per problem statement's note, but the treemap proportional-cell layout is dominated by these synthetic clients — consider commercial_name disambiguation (e.g. include the suffix or org_id last-4) so admins can tell them apart at a glance.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Seed ops@/compliance@/support@prosper.foundation in seed.py with their intended (non-super_admin) roles so future RBAC tests can assert 403 paths on super-admin-only endpoints (retry-step, etc.). Today only client_admin can be used to assert 403, which is fine but narrow.
OPTIONAL: Display a disambiguation token next to the many 'TEST Holdings' rows on the by-client and volume-by-client tables (e.g. org_id last-4 in muted text). Cosmetic only.

OPTIONAL: Verify by-client DataTable renders all rows — initial Playwright pass observed only 1 tbody row but the underlying API returns many. Likely a non-issue (DataTable may use a non-tbody render path), but worth a manual eyeball.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/operations.py is clean. _scrub helper is defined but unused — minor. The `only_errors` filter overwrites any user-provided $or (search) by concatenating into q['$or'] — this is benign because search uses $or only and is checked first, but when BOTH search and only_errors are passed the final $or is the union of all four search regexes + 2 status branches, which is the intended behavior. Verified by reading L72-83.

operations.py funds_state synthesizes treasury_balance as `supply * 0.08`. The endpoint contract says treasury_usd is sourced from Stellar; the synthetic computation is correctly documented inline. Once Stellar egress is opened, replace with a real Horizon /accounts query.
operations.py upstream_status returns reachable=False unconditionally. The note string documents this. When wiring the real probe, gate it behind a 2s timeout so the 3-LED UI doesn't stall.

operations.py retry_step does NOT check if the step is currently in 'error' or 'pending' before flipping — it will happily reset 'ok' or 'skipped' steps to pending too. Add a guard or accept the current behavior intentionally (the spec doesn't require it but a defensive check would prevent operator footguns).

operations.py by_client_stats sparkline assembles raw daily counts but doesn't pad zero-days, so a sparkline of an org with sparse activity has fewer than 30 points. The UI renders it as a polyline so visually it still works, but consider zero-padding so all sparklines have the same x-scale.

server.py L192 + L239 — auto-promote-to-super_admin-by-domain is a sharp edge. In production any newly-onboarded prosper.foundation employee instantly gets full god-mode on first login. Recommend gating super_admin behind an explicit allowlist (or default new domain users to role=admin and require an existing super_admin to elevate them).
